base_prompt: Explain why deleting a shortcut from a computer's desktop usually does not uninstall the application. A response of around 160 words is enough.
text: Deleting a shortcut from a computer’s desktop usually does not uninstall the application because a shortcut is only a small link or pointer to the program, not the program itself. It tells the operating system where to find the application’s executable file and may include settings such as startup options or an icon. The actual application is normally stored elsewhere, such as in the “Program Files” folder on Windows or the “Applications” folder on macOS. Removing the shortcut simply removes that convenient way to launch the program; it does not delete the application’s files, libraries, settings, or data. The program may still be opened through the Start menu, Applications folder, search feature, or another shortcut. To uninstall it properly, users should use the operating system’s uninstall feature, such as “Apps & Features” or “Add or Remove Programs” in Windows, or an application-specific uninstaller. On macOS, applications can often be moved to the Trash, although additional support files may remain.
